As part of this commitment, Africa CDC has established the Africa CDC Reference Laboratory, a continental Centre of Excellence for Diagnostics, Research, and Innovation (CEDRI). The Africa CDC Reference Laboratory plays a critical role in supporting laboratory networks across Member States by providing technical assistance to National Public Health Laboratories (NPHLs), particularly where diagnostic capacity is limited and advanced testing is required for emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases. This support enhances the continent’s ability to detect, respond to, and prepare for public health threats, including high-consequence pathogens such as Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV). The positions will be based in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Republic of Uganda, and the Republic of South Sudan. Serving as key liaisons between their respective National Public Health Laboratories (NPHLs) and the Africa CDC Reference Laboratory, these locally recruited professionals will strengthen laboratory systems, improve sample referral and management processes, support proficiency testing programs, and enhance outbreak detection and response capacities. Their deployment will further strengthen collaboration between national and continental laboratory networks, contributing to timely disease detection, effective outbreak response, and improved preparedness for public health emergencies across Africa. The Molecular Virologists will serve as key links between the NPHLs and the Africa CDC Reference Laboratory, ensuring effective coordination, timely sample referral and testing, and the exchange of critical laboratory information. Through the provision of advanced technical expertise, they will strengthen national laboratory capacity, enhance diagnostic and sequencing capabilities, and support timely detection, characterization, and response to public health threats. Facilitate timely communication and reporting of laboratory results, testing volumes, and operational challenges to support evidence-based outbreak response decision-making. Employee Contract Type Local - Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term) Job Description Job Purpose : The Clinical Nurse will responsible to under-take planning, implementing, monitoring, and reporting primary health care and nutrition interventions at woreda, health facility, community, and IDP site levels. The position holder will strengthen the quality of health and nutrition services through direct service provision, capacity building, technical support, supervision, and coordination with government health structures and community stakeholders. Conduct patient assessment, triage, treatment, stabilization, referral, and follow-up according to national treatment guidelines. title: Senior Project Associate (LMI)
description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates. Organizational Context and Scope IOM Ethiopia’s Migration Management and Government (MMG) Unit works closely with the Government of Ethiopia, and various stakeholders to contribute to addressing the migration governnance needs, as well as to promote and uphold the rights of individuals and their communities. The Unit has three main areas of intervention: Coordination and Capacity Development support (CCD), Immigration and border governance (IBG), and Labor Mobility and Social Inclusion (LMI). IOM’ Ethiopia Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion programme provides policy, regulatory and operational guidance in matters related to labour and human mobility facilitation, integration and social cohesion, and diaspora engagement as an enabler of sustainable development in line with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Under the overall supervision of the Senior Migration Management and Governance Officer, and the direct supervision of the National Programme Officer (LMI), the Senior Project Associate (Labor Migration and Social Inclusion – LMI) will support the technical, operational and administrative implementation of Labor Mobility and Social Inclusion projects within the LMI portfolio. The incumbent will serve as the operational technical focal point for Youth Business Incubator (YBI) initiatives and will support other labor migration and social inclusion -related initiatives implemented under the LMI portfolio. The incumbent will provide technical coordination support under the guidance of the National Programme Officer LMI, in alignment with approved project documents, donor requirements and IOM standards. Responsibilities Assist in the planning, coordination, implementation and monitoring of project activities. Compile, summarise, analyse, and present information/data on specific project topics, highlighting noteworthy issues for the consideration of appropriate parties. Monitor budget implementation and propose adjustments as necessary. Act as focal point for administrative coordination of project implementation, involving extensive liaison with diverse organisational units and external parties to initiate requests, obtain necessary clearances, follow-up on administrative actions, etc. Draft status reports, identify shortfalls, bring them to the attention of the supervisor and suggest corrective measures to address delivery gaps. Draft correspondence on project issues, prepare and update reports, briefing notes, graphics, statistical tables, and other forms of documentation. Organise meetings, workshops and training sessions, prepare training materials and participate in the delivering of capacity building workshops. Respond to complex information requests and inquiries. Set up and maintain files/records. Participate in meetings and conferences. Maintain effective liaison and coordination with local authorities, partners, United Nation (UN) agencies, intergovernmental and non-governmental organisations, donors and other stakeholders relevant to the project. Monitor work of implementing partners and report any non-compliance to the supervisor. Provide inputs for the development of Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and concept papers and provide general support for the development of new projects. Provides guidance/training and assist in coordinating and monitoring work of other staff in the unit. May supervise other staff as assigned. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.
